intended_object: The complex of global sections Γ(X, C^•(F)) of the canonical (Godement) flasque resolution of an abelian sheaf F on a topological space X. Its cohomology computes the sheaf cohomology H^n(X, F). Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and how the library uses it (the homology comparisons that follow it).
explanation:
The flasque envelope here is G(F) = ∏_x skyscraper_x(F_x), the product of the skyscraper sheaves on the stalks, with the adjunction unit F → G(F). The resolution is built by iterating Q = coker(F → G(F)): degree n is G(Qⁿ F), and the differential is G(Qⁿ F) → Q^{n+1} F → G(Q^{n+1} F). This is exactly Godement's canonical flasque resolution: C⁰ = G(F), Z¹ = coker, C¹ = G(Z¹), and so on.

`terminalSectionsFunctor` evaluates a sheaf on ⊤ = X, so it is the global-sections functor Γ(X, –). The definition applies Γ(X, –) termwise to this cochain complex via `mapHomologicalComplex`, which gives Γ(X, C^•(F)) as intended.

Mathlib has no Godement resolution: a search of Mathlib for "Godement" found nothing.

The only restriction is that X is in `TopCat.{0}` with `AddCommGrpCat.{0}` coefficients. This is a universe-monomorphism choice made for the whole library and acknowledged in the module documentation. It is a Lean technicality, not a narrower mathematical setting: the definition already works for every topological space and every abelian sheaf. So the definition is faithful.
